entry.label: Emergence
entry.description: The appearance at one scale of properties, patterns or capacities not straightforwardly present at another scale, arising through interactions and organisation. It describes a relation across levels; it is not a hidden causal substance.
entry.canonical_definition: A relation across levels or scales in which a macro-property or pattern arises from interactions among lower-level components yet is not usefully reducible to a simple inventory of those components.

profile.title: Emergence
profile.canonical_definition: A relation across levels or scales in which a macro-property or pattern arises from interactions among lower-level components yet is not usefully reducible to a simple inventory of those components.
profile.summary: Emergence names a relation across levels: interactions among parts produce a pattern, property or capacity visible at another scale. It can mark genuine explanatory work, but the word becomes empty when used instead of specifying mechanisms and conditions.
profile.why_it_matters: Complex outcomes cannot usually be attributed to one actor or intervention. Emergence helps resist linear claims of delivery and control. It does not mean outcomes are uncaused, magical or beyond all inquiry.
key_distinctions: weak or epistemic emergence vs stronger ontological claims
novel pattern vs surprise to an observer
practice_connections: stop claiming to deliver outcomes produced by many interacting agents
look for conditions and feedback rather than single causes
state the scale at which the property appears
use experiments and probes without pretending they command the whole
profile.editorial_note: Readable orientation and evidence-backed first pass. Not accepted scholarly consensus until named review is recorded.
